en: Khuddakapāṭha 6:
Ratana Sutta Whatever beings have gathered here,
May all beings, whether those on earth or those in the sky,
be well-disposed toward one another,
and may they also listen attentively to what is said.
Therefore, all you beings, listen well:
practice loving-kindness toward the human race;
for day and night they carry offerings to you.
Therefore, being heedful, protect them.
Whatever wealth there is here or in the world beyond,
or whatever exquisite jewel exists in the heavens;
There is no one equal to the Tathāgata;
this too is the sublime jewel in the Buddha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
The destruction, dispassion, the deathless, the sublime—
what the concentrated Sakyan Sage attained:
there is nothing equal to that Dhamma.
This too is the sublime treasure of the Dhamma;
by this truth, may there be well-being.
That purity which the Best of Buddhas has praised—
They call the immediate concentration "the one without interval";
there exists nothing equal to that concentration.
This too is a sublime treasure among the Dhamma.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Those eight persons who are praised by the virtuous consist of these four pairs.
They are the disciples of the Sugata, worthy of offerings;
gifts given to them yield great fruit.
This too is the sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being for those who are well-applied with a firm mind,
striving without retreat in the teaching of Gotama.
Having reached the goal, having plunged into the Deathless,
and enjoying the peace they have won for free—
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Just as a pillar fixed in the earth would be unshakable by the four winds;
I speak of the true person as being like that,
who sees the noble truths through direct knowledge;
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being for those who discern the Noble Truths,
so well-taught by the one of profound wisdom.
Even if they are exceedingly negligent,
they do not take up an eighth existence;
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Together with the attainment of vision,
these three qualities are abandoned by him:
Personalistic view, doubt,
and whatever there may be of mere rules and observances—
he is completely liberated from the four states of misery.
There are six things that cannot be done;
this too is a sublime treasure in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Even if he should perform an evil deed by body, speech, or mind,
he is incapable of concealing it.
The incapacity of one who has seen the Truth has been declared;
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Just as a forest grove is in full bloom at its peak in the first month of summer, during the heat of the season,
even so did he teach the sublime Dhamma.
Leading to Nibbāna, for the supreme welfare;
this too is the sublime jewel in the Buddha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
The Excellent One, who knows the excellent, the Giver of the excellent, the Bearer of the excellent,
the Unsurpassed One, has taught the excellent Dhamma;
this too is the sublime Jewel in the Buddha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
The old is destroyed, and there is no new arising;
their minds are dispassionate toward future existence.
With their seeds destroyed and no longer desiring growth,
these wise ones are extinguished like this lamp;
this too is a sublime jewel in the Saṅgha.
By this truth, may there be well-being.
Whatever beings have gathered here,
whether they belong to the earth or to the atmosphere;
To the Tathāgata, honored by gods and humans, to the Buddha we pay homage; may there be well-being.
Whatever beings have gathered here—
Whether they be of the earth or those in the sky,
let us pay homage to the Tathāgata, honored by gods and humans, and to the Dhamma; may there be well-being.
Whatever beings have gathered here,
whether of the earth or those in the sky,
[behold] the Tathāgata, honored by gods and men.
We pay homage to the Saṅgha; may there be well-being.
Thus ends the Ratana Sutta.
